image.alt: A Monstera deliciosa with large glossy leaves split into deep lobes, in a white pot

items: Trained up a tree trunk or totem

snap: A dramatic statement houseplant famous for its large, glossy leaves naturally split with architectural holes and climbing, jungle-like growth.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: Native to tropical rainforests of southern Mexico and Central America; grows as a climbing vine with large split leaves reaching 6–8 feet tall indoors on support.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top 2 inches of soil dry out; provide a moss pole or trellis for aerial roots to attach and climb.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The holes and splits — fenestrations — arrive as the plant matures and climbs, not on a young plant, and brighter light brings them on sooner. Give it a moss pole and the leaves get larger and more deeply cut; leave it unsupported and it stays small-leaved and sprawling.
